newsitem.title: POLAND: ZLOTY LINGERS NEAR RESISTANCE LEVELS, C.BANK QUIET.
newsitem.headline: ZLOTY LINGERS NEAR RESISTANCE LEVELS, C.BANK QUIET.

text.p: Polish zloty toyed with central bank intervention levels but did not set off any central bank buying interventions during mostly listless Tuesday trade.
Dealers said that although a light currency-selling sentiment remained on the market, trade lacked large client orders which would push the zloty decisively above resistance.
"The zloty tracked dollar/mark moves as no fundementals to push it higher appeared on Tuesday, but the market's pro-zloty mood remained intact," said Piort Czyzewski, dealer at ING bank in Warsaw.
The zloty closed at 1.56/1.52 percent from the trading band centre, up from Monday's 1.49/1.38 percent close and just above the central bank's last intervention level at 1.45 percent.
It closed at 3.2190/00 to the dollar, flat from 3.2185/00 on Monday and at 1.8647/57 to the mark, up from 1.8655/89.
Dealers said however that if foreign investors place large amounts of bids for Polish fixed bonds at Wednesday's 800 million zloty tender, the zloty would again push upward.
"If foreigners are active at tomorrow's tender, the zloty could again try to break resistance levels and will likely set off a central bank intervention," one foreign bank dealer said.

Dealers said the central bank did not intervene on Tuesday, after buying an estimated $60 million on Friday and Monday combined because the market was basically balanced and upward pressure on the zloty was light during today's session.
At tomorrow's fixed bond tender the 15-percent two-year bond's yield was expected to form around 21.10-21.15 percent and the 12-percent five-year yield around 18.45-18.50 percent.
On the money market both overnight and tomorrow/next rates closed at 22.30/22.60 pct, flat at bid and slightly higher at offer than this morning.
